basics.name: Kenneth Neal
basics.label: Lead Innovation Engineer
basics.summary: Lead Innovation Engineer at Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana with over a decade of experience spanning infrastructure operations, database administration, and site reliability engineering. Recognized inside the organization as the go-to technical authority for Infrastructure and Operations, routinely advising management on priorities, design alternatives, and vendor decisions. Built and operate the batch job approval-and-execution platform used across I&O, automated infrastructure monitoring and decommissioning workflows with PowerShell and API integrations, and led HA/DR architecture for the company's core claims-processing systems. President of Baton Rouge User Groups, the nonprofit overseeing Baton Rouge's SQL, .NET, and Analytics user groups, and Chair of the Baton Rouge SQL Saturday Planning Committee.

work.name: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana
work.summary: Promoted to Lead Innovation Engineer in March 2026, extending prior SRE responsibilities for Infrastructure and Operations while building rapid, AI-assisted solutions to operational problems.
highlights: Continue to serve as the senior technical authority for Infrastructure and Operations processes and technology, advising management on priorities and technical alternatives.
Use AI-assisted development tools to rapidly prototype and ship quick-win internal applications that close operational gaps for I&O and business partners.
Own and extend the batch job approval-and-execution platform and infrastructure automation workflows built during the SRE role.

work.name: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana
work.summary: Served as the senior technical authority for Infrastructure and Operations, driving monitoring, batch processing, and infrastructure automation improvements across the estate.
highlights: Served as the senior technical expert for Infrastructure and Operations processes and technology, presenting priorities and technical alternatives to management and cross-functional teams.
Designed and built a custom ServiceNow application to govern batch job systems end-to-end, replacing manual approval and execution with automated, auditable API-driven workflows.
Worked hands-on with Control-M for batch job scheduling and SolarWinds/SCOM for infrastructure monitoring as part of I&O's monitoring and batch platforms.

Streamlined and automated the infrastructure deprovisioning process using PowerShell and API calls, reducing the time to complete a decommission request by 99% and improving overall infrastructure availability and hygiene.
Met regularly with other teams to scope and plan automation projects that reduced operational toil for I&O staff.

work.name: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana
work.summary: Architected and deployed SQL Server environments, ensuring HA/DR requirements were met while automating upgrades to the company's main claims processing system.
highlights: Architected and deployed SQL Server environments and ensured that HA and DR requirements were met, maintaining security, backup, and redundancy strategies for critical claims infrastructure.
Proactively monitored the SQL Server estate for health and performance, identifying bottlenecks and working with developers to resolve them before end users were impacted.

Designed and automated the deployment and upgrading of the company's main claims processing system, accomplishing upgrades and infrastructure refreshes in minutes instead of hours to maximize system availability.
Automated the deployment of a full DR environment for use in disaster recovery drills, validating recovery and redundancy procedures.
Worked across teams to streamline processes and manage internal customer requests in a timely manner, providing 2nd- and 3rd-level technical support.
Served as backup to the Oracle DBA.
Recognized multiple times with a SPOT award for going above and beyond to serve customers.

work.name: Amedisys
work.summary: Responsible for over 300 SQL Server instances, ensuring performance and high availability of critical databases.
highlights: Responsible for over 300 SQL Server instances, managing and monitoring installed systems and infrastructure across the estate.
Actively monitored production system performance for potential bottlenecks and worked with other groups to correct issues before end users were impacted.
Reviewed code from developers to ensure that queries were optimal before being released to production.
Ensured that critical databases were configured for high availability.

projects.name: Day of Data Baton Rouge

projects.entity: Baton Rouge SQL Server User Group
highlights: Chair the Baton Rouge SQL Saturday Planning Committee, coordinating speakers, sponsors, and volunteers over months of planning each year.
Helped grow the event into a full day of free training drawing Louisiana IT and data professionals for learning, networking, and mentorship.

references.name: Ryan LeBlanc
references.reference: Kenny is invaluable to any team environment. He is able to communicate very well in any setting and excels in talking about technologies. He is able to keep up with today's technologies and collaborate with the team on solutions to problems that arise. He is an invaluable DBA to have and he is able to accomplish tasks very fast. Kenny is able to add a sense of light humor to the workplace that lightens the mood and makes it feel less like a 9 to 5 painful job and more like a down to earth enjoyable place to get stuff done and collaborate. His professionalism when it comes to getting things done is second to none.
